name: visual-a
thesis: Forge Next should look like an instrument panel built inside the approved TNR character: a dark, dense, high-contrast console over layered navy where every lifecycle state is a labelled lamp (glyph + text + fill/hollow, never colour alone), where the three things that can touch the live game - a live write, a publish, an unconfirmed send - each own one hue AND one construction that nothing else may use (crimson ink button, parchment ink button, dashed violet), and where polish comes from depth, warm ivory typography, tabular counters and short transitions on progress, never from motion on state. Today's Forge already has the right bones (scoped CSSOM tokens, 44px taps, AA contrast everywhere) but paints risk with the same vocabulary as everything else; this direction keeps the bones, adopts the approved crimson/gold/blue-over-navy family and the game's own hard-edged ink control, and fixes the vocabulary.

proposal.one_line: A dense, dark-first TNR operations console: layered navy surfaces, warm ivory ink, every lifecycle state a labelled lamp, and the three things that can touch production (live write, publish, unconfirmed send) each owning one hue AND one construction that nothing else in the app may use.
proposal.relationship_to_the_approved_direction: This is direction A elaborated inside the approved character (amendment sections 2-3, 12): deep navy/charcoal ground, crimson/gold/cool-blue accent family, ivory/parchment reserved for high-attention surfaces, hard-edged ink controls used selectively, layered depth, controlled motion, explicit READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY contexts (section 8). What it changes with rationale (section 12 "illustrative"): exact hex values, the mockup's photographic lane art and hero landscape (replaced by CSS washes and SVG glyphs - runtime assets are banned and embedded raster costs every game page, H_RISK_REGISTER R-06), the crimson active-nav marker (blue, so crimson stays the write signal), and the five saturated quick-action fills (rails + glyphs, so filled colour stays reserved for lamps and the three production controls). Each of those is listed under user_decisions_surfaced rather than settled silently.

design_tokens.mechanism: CSS custom properties declared on .f-host and .f-app exactly as styles.mjs:11,19-20 does today (never :root, per the scoping law at styles.mjs:3-9), light overrides on .f-host[data-theme=light]. Every hex below was measured with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (sRGB linearisation, (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05)) by the script that generated this file; thresholds: 4.5:1 for all text including 12px/600 lamp text (not "large"), 3:1 for non-text boundaries, rails, focus rings and track segments (1.4.11).

hue_assignment.--acc cool chakra blue: system/active accent (amendment section 3): interactive, CONFIRMED, RUNNING, focus ring, active nav marker, item-track current outline
hue_assignment.--read sky blue: READ ONLY mode and its control; same family as --acc so "blue = reads/system/safe" is one lesson
hue_assignment.--mut crimson (fill) + --mut-ink rose (t: LIVE WRITE only, plus the brand slash in the wordmark. Crimson is a SURFACE colour (2.67:1 against paper, so it is never used as small text and never as a boundary); its text form is the rose --mut-ink (8.99:1 on paper)
hue_assignment.--pub parchment + --on-pub: PUBLISH mode, the publish control and the PUBLISHED lamp: the only light surface in the dark UI (14.41:1 against paper)
hue_assignment.--gold: admin/review cues (amendment section 3): Content Admin nav badge, DRAFT lamp, review-queue rails, brand tagline. Never a warning
hue_assignment.--warn amber: caution and RECOVERY: PAUSED, INCOMPLETE, ORPHANED (filled), rate-limit halt, drift
hue_assignment.--sent violet: unconfirmed request only (allowed decorative lane colour, amendment section 3; it overrides no semantic colour)
hue_assignment.--ok green / --bad coral: semantic success / danger only: VERIFIED, FAILED, ABORTED, SIGNED OUT, TRIPPED
hue_assignment.adjacency_warning: crimson-rose (--mut-ink) and coral (--bad) are hue neighbours (1.39:1 between them), as are gold and amber (1.1:1). The approved character asks for both crimson and semantic red, and both gold and semantic amber, so the panel separates them by CONSTRUCTION (crimson only as a filled ink button/strip; --bad only as lamp/text; gold only hollow; amber filled for ORPHANED) and by the label and glyph that every state carries. This is surfaced as a director decision below rather than resolved by dropping an approved hue.

pill_lamps_dark.rule: A lamp is a 3px-radius rectangle, 12px/600, letter-spacing .04em, an inline SVG glyph (createElementNS, aria-hidden, 12px) before the exact journal state word, min-height 24px. HOLLOW = transient or neutral: 1px border and text in the state colour on the state's tint. FILLED = final, or demands the operator now: background in the state colour, dark on-fill text. Exactly one lamp uses a DASHED border (SENT) and exactly one uses a parchment fill (PUBLISHED). Risk states carry a suffix so the word itself says why it matters. Lamps never animate (amendment section 9; non-negotiable).

typography.family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif (resolves to Roboto or Samsung One on the operator's Samsung Firefox; nothing is fetched). Mono: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Roboto Mono', monospace for ids, hashes, keys, procedure paths and journal text only (amendment section 11). font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on .f-app so counters, budgets and countdowns never jitter - the single most 'instrument' typographic decision.
typography.brand: The FORGE wordmark is system-ui 800, uppercase, letter-spacing .14em, --ink, with a crimson (--brand-crimson) diagonal slash drawn as one inline SVG path (createElementNS) behind the R, and the tagline 'CREATE · VALIDATE · DEPLOY' in 10px/600 --gold tracking .18em. No display face is fetched (non-negotiable); if the director wants the mockup's brushed logotype, it must be vector letterforms embedded as SVG paths (about 1.5 KB) and is a separate art decision.

typography.weights: 400 body, 500 key labels in kv grids, 600 lamps/buttons/h2/mode strips, 700 titles and counters, 800 wordmark and hero only. No 300 anywhere: thin weights lose on AMOLED in sunlight.

typography.why_it_reads_at_390_in_daylight: Ink on paper is 14.77:1 and secondary text is held to 8.29:1 (AAA) rather than the 4.5 floor, because glare eats the bottom of the contrast range first. The floor is 12px and only in 600 weight or mono; body is 15px/1.4 giving about 48ch per line at 366px content width, inside the 45-75ch comfort band. Uppercase is limited to 11px eyebrows with .08em tracking; long strings (ids, paths) are mono with word-break so nothing overflows the viewport. Sizes are px on .f-app, not rem, because rem would bind Forge to the game document's root font-size (globals.css:223 at the pin sets html font-size: calc(12px * var(--font-scale))), which the scoping law at styles.mjs:3-9 forbids; Firefox Android's own text zoom still scales px. Warm ivory (--ink #efeae0) rather than pure white keeps the parchment kinship the amendment asks for without losing luminance (it is within 2% of #ffffff's).

animates: screen swap: the new screen is mounted at opacity 0 and driven to 1 in 120ms; the old screen is removed synchronously so content is present in the DOM from t=0 (motion never delays state)
lane card / quick action: --glow-active ring and a 1px lift (translateY(-1px)) over 150ms on :focus-visible and :active (no hover dependence); static once settled

aggregate progress: the item track's summary bar width, transition 200ms; requires the track element to be updated in place rather than rebuilt by the 1.5s replace() tick (app.mjs:268, dom.mjs:27), otherwise the transition restarts every tick

running sweep: a 2px bar under the mode strip with a 1.2s linear translateX loop in --acc, present only while app.state.running === jobId and removed synchronously on any other state; decoration on top of the RUNNING lamp, never the only indicator
details expansion (advanced metadata, drift lists): 160ms grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr; content is in the DOM and focusable from t=0
button press: transform scale(.98) for 80ms on :active; the two hard-edged production buttons instead translate 2px into their offset shadow (the game's ink-button press, globals.css:281-283)
toast enter: translateY(8px) to 0 with opacity, 150ms; toasts never animate out (removal is instant)
confirm sheet: backdrop opacity 120ms; the sheet's content is static and rendered before the backdrop starts
motion.durations_easing: 80ms (press), 120ms (fades), 150ms (glow/lift), 160ms (expand), 200ms (progress); cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1) throughout; nothing longer than 200ms except the sweep loop
motion.reduced_motion: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) scoped as .f-app *, .f-app *::before, .f-app *::after { transition-duration: 0ms !important; animation: none !important } plus the sweep element hidden; the RUNNING lamp, the readout numbers and the track already carry the state. Because whether Firefox Android forwards the OS "Remove animations" setting is unverified, Settings also gets a "Reduce motion" toggle that sets data-motion=reduce on .f-host (stored in localStorage under tnr_forge_ui_v1) and applies the same rules.
never_animates: lamps (pills), including their appearance, colour and text
verdict lamps, halt cards and mode strips (READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY) - they appear and disappear instantly
the session lamp and the auth banner
the UNCONFIRMED strip, SENT stripes, ORPHANED cards
budget gauges and numbers (step instantly; no counting up)
the readout counters on the item track
disabled-to-enabled on Write / Publish / Reconcile / Resume buttons (a button that fades in arrives late)
confirm sheet text and the record list inside it
nav badges, the Content Admin pending count, and the brand block
anything fading OUT: a risk state is removed the instant the state changes, never eased away

risk_states.mutation_screen: Today: the preflight card's primary button is the same blue .f-primary (styles.mjs:33) for 'Run captures' and 'Start job' (screens.mjs:151-156); the only distinction is prose inside window.confirm (app.mjs:172-175). Proposed: the whole preflight/run screen takes LIVE WRITE: a 3px --mut-ink bar at the very top of the top bar, the LIVE WRITE mode strip with counts, the h2 prefixed with the hammer glyph, and the primary control becomes the crimson ink button (radius 0, --mut fill, 2px --ink border, --on-mut text 6.17:1, 3px 3px 0 --mut-ink offset) labelled with the count and the verb: 'Write 12 items to the game'. Read-only manifests take READ ONLY and a rounded --read button 'Run 5 reads · zero mutations'. The two differ in hue, construction, geometry, strip and text; nothing about them can be confused at a glance or by a colour-blind operator.
risk_states.publish_action: Publish gets the one light surface in the dark UI and the strictest shape: the PUBLISH mode strip on parchment with a crimson rule, and a full-width parchment ink button (the game's ink-primary construction, globals.css:265-271, re-tokenised) that is disabled until the sheet has rendered three facts - which records, their current lamp (HIDDEN), and that the session lamp is READY - then a custom confirm sheet (replacing window.confirm, which cannot show lamps) repeats the record names and lamps and offers exactly one parchment 'Publish 2 records to players' and one neutral 'Cancel'. After the tap the rows show SENT · unconfirmed until the read-back, then PUBLISHED · live (the same parchment construction) or FAILED. Nothing about publish is one-tap; a polished interface must not turn publish into an accidental tap (amendment section 7).
risk_states.ambiguous_sent: Today: SENT is a hollow purple pill beside a hollow blue CONFIRMED (styles.mjs:43), the open-job banner is a generic warn banner (screens.mjs:18-26) and its Resume button is the same blue as Start. Proposed: (1) the SENT lamp is the only dashed-border lamp and reads 'SENT · unconfirmed'; (2) its row is striped with --stripe-sent (static; ink still 9.71:1 over the stripe); (3) a sticky UNCONFIRMED strip in --tint-sent appears under the mode strip on every screen while any job holds a SENT item, with the one action 'Reconcile · reads only, never re-sends' as the dashed violet square button; (4) the Home card for that job carries a violet rail and the RECOVERY strip; (5) the item track shows the arrow-with-gap segment. Five redundant cues, none colour-only, and no control on the screen is labelled or shaped like 'send again'.
risk_states.paused_or_orphaned: Today: paused jobs are a warn banner, bad only for SESSION and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS (screens.mjs:208-219); ORPHANED shares amber with PAUSED and INCOMPLETE (styles.mjs:45). Proposed: the screen enters RECOVERY (amber strip with counts) and a halt card replaces the banner - full width, 4px rail, tint background, an --fs-5 title naming the reason from the journal's pause vocabulary (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:93) and a tabular countdown where one exists: USER and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS in --warn ('HALTED · rate limit on jutsu.getAll · retry allowed in 00:41'), SESSION in --bad ('HALTED · signed out · nothing further was sent'), AMBIGUOUS/ORPHANED in filled --warn ('HALTED · a write may have landed · decide below'). ORPHANED items get the only filled amber lamp in the system, an amber rail and a card headed 'Needs a decision', pinned to the top of the Command Center and counted in a nav badge, so an orphan is visible from every screen, not only from Jobs.
risk_states.auth_and_role: Three separate looks for three separate problems (amendment section 9): SIGNED OUT = filled --bad session lamp + --tint-bad banner; NOT AUTHORIZED (the account lacks the role a Content Admin action needs) = hollow --warn lamp + --tint-warn banner naming the action, never a generic error; READ FAILED = --bad text on the item row only. The session lamp never turns amber for a transport failure and never turns red for a missing role.
risk_states.toasts: Today a 'bad' toast auto-removes after 9000ms (app.mjs:100). Proposed: ok/info toasts auto-dismiss at 4s; warn/bad toasts persist until tapped and stack; anything that also changed a lamp is already visible in the lamp, so a missed toast never hides state.

light_dark.support: Both. Dark is the default and the design target (the approved character is dark; the operator's phone is an AMOLED Samsung; the lamps are built on light-on-dark); light exists for direct sunlight and for a Content Admin working on a bright desktop.
light_dark.mechanism: Two token sets on .f-host/.f-app (dark) and .f-host[data-theme=light] (light), color-scheme set alongside so native controls follow; a Settings control "Theme: dark / light / auto" stored in localStorage under tnr_forge_ui_v1; "auto" applies a scoped @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) .f-host:not([data-theme]) override. No :root, no document-level rule (styles.mjs:3-9). Every pair in both sets is listed with its ratio; the light set is AA throughout and AAA on ink.
light_dark.light_specifics: In light the crimson and gold move to their dark forms (crimson #9e1b2a is both fill and text; gold #7d5f0e is text only), the parchment publish surface keeps its hue but gains a 2px --on-pub border because parchment on white is 1.19:1, and the SENT stripe goes to #cfc0f2 under ink text (the SENT lamp sits on its own --tint-sent box, so no lamp text ever sits on the stripe).

what_it_borrows_from_the_game.source: app/src/styles/globals.css read at game head 36c5873b (the head this plan pinned, A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:133); the ink-button block is byte-identical at the Forge pin 345d18ac (lines 243, 265 in both).
borrowed: The ink-button construction: .tnr-ink-btn-primary (globals.css:265-271) is a parchment #f8f1dc fill, a 2px #26110c border, radius 0 and a 5px 5px 0 #b7331f crimson offset shadow; on hover it translates 2px into the shadow (:281-283) and its focus ring is a 2px parchment outline at 4px offset (:296-300). Forge's PUBLISH control is exactly this construction re-tokenised (--pub fill, --on-pub border, 4px 4px 0 --mut). LIVE WRITE inverts it (crimson fill, ivory border and text, rose offset), the way .tnr-ink-btn-secondary (:273-279) inverts the primary (dark #070b12 fill, parchment border, blue offset). The game uses a blue offset on its secondary; Forge uses rose so that blue stays the read/system colour.

The dark-mode ground: the game's .dark --background is 222 47% 11% (globals.css:138), a navy in the same hue as Forge's --paper #121827, so the overlay reads as kin to the game's own dark mode rather than a foreign grey box.
The 8px radius (--radius 0.5rem, globals.css:134) for cards and sheets.
considered_and_not_borrowed: The .tnr-pixel-clip notched corners (globals.css:226-241): considered for the brand block only; rejected for controls because notches cost hit area and read as game chrome around safety-critical actions (amendment section 3 last paragraph).
The parchment page ground of the light theme (--background 55 92% 95%, globals.css:101): a warm page would blur the overlay boundary and collapse red/amber/orange into the page palette.
The 12px root font-size (globals.css:223): the overlay uses px on .f-app for the scoping reason above.
Any illustration, franchise-adjacent imagery or copied identity (amendment section 3).

rejected_alternatives: Neon/cyberpunk glow console: glows and blooms reduce edge contrast, cost paint on mobile Firefox, and make amber/orange/red read as one warm smear.

Skinning Forge in the game's parchment palette: it would make the overlay look like the game and hide the "this is a tool above the game" boundary the takeover model depends on (takeover.mjs header comment).
Crimson as the active-nav marker (as in the mockup): it spends the write signal on navigation; blue is the amendment's own "active accent".
Filled saturated quick-action cards (as in the mockup): five fills compete with the lamps and make the one crimson control less special; rails and glyphs carry the lane identity instead.

Photographic lane art and a hero landscape (as in the mockup): runtime-fetched assets are banned and embedded raster would be parsed on every game page (R-06); a static CSS wash gives atmosphere at zero bytes of asset.
Gold text on the parchment publish surface: 1.38:1, unreadable; the publish strip uses --on-pub text and a crimson rule instead.
Gold-filled publish button: it would put publish and caution (amber) in the same construction; parchment is unmistakable and is the game's own ink-primary.
Monochrome with one accent: five risk lanes plus ok/warn/bad need more than one reserved hue; encoding them by shape alone fails at 12px on a phone.
Pulsing or blinking SENT/ORPHANED lamps: violates "pills never animate", and reduced-motion would erase the very signal it was meant to add; static stripes plus a dashed border carry it instead.
Hold-to-confirm for publish: duration-dependent, hostile to switch access and to a sweaty thumb in sunlight; a two-step sheet with explicit facts is safer and no slower.
999px rounded pills as today (styles.mjs:42): they read as decorative tags; rectangular lamps with glyphs read as instruments.
rem-based type scale: binds the overlay to the game document's root font size, which the scoping law forbids.
Glass/backdrop-filter surfaces: expensive on Android Firefox and they lower contrast under the blur.
A fetched display font for the wordmark: forbidden; an SVG vector wordmark is the only route and is a separate art decision.

accessibility.focus: Every focusable element gets :focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--focus) } - a 2px gap halo in the surface colour then a 2px --focus ring (8.62:1 on paper dark, 6.27:1 light, both >=3). The two hard-edged ink controls keep their offset shadow under the ring. Item-track segments and lamps that act as buttons get the same ring; nothing relies on outline colour inheritance from the game.
accessibility.colour_blind_redundancy: Every lamp = colour + glyph + exact state word (+ suffix for risk states) + fill/hollow + border style (dashed only for SENT) + row rail; SENT rows additionally striped. Every mode = strip position + glyph + the words READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY + counts. Every production control = geometry (square vs rounded) + offset shadow + verb-and-count label. Under deuteranopia crimson/coral and gold/amber lose their hue difference but not their construction difference: the write button is the only dark square with a light border, the publish button the only light square, ORPHANED the only filled amber, FAILED always carries the cross. Verdicts are sentences ("Finished UNVERIFIED", "Verified: every item read back equal") as today (screens.mjs:200-206), never a coloured dot alone.
accessibility.semantics: Lamps are spans with the state text as content (no aria-label needed); the SVG glyph is aria-hidden. Mode strips and halt cards have role=status / role=alert; the UNCONFIRMED strip has role=status aria-live=polite; toasts are appended to an aria-live=polite region (bad toasts assertive). Nav uses aria-current=page as today (app.mjs:84); the bottom nav is a nav element with a list. Buttons say what they do ("Write 12 items to the game", "Reconcile · reads only, never re-sends", "Publish 2 records to players") so screen-reader users get the risk in the name.
accessibility.touch_and_keyboard: 44px minimum everywhere, 48px nav and action bar, 52px production controls; no hover-only affordance (glow appears on focus-visible and active); the confirm sheet traps focus and closes on Escape and on Cancel only, never on backdrop tap for write/publish sheets; details/summary keep native keyboard behaviour; the More sheet on the phone is a dialog with a visible Close.
accessibility.text_and_zoom: px sizes on .f-app with a 12px floor; long mono strings wrap (word-break); Firefox Android text zoom scales the panel; no fixed-height text containers, so 200% zoom reflows instead of clipping; the bottom nav labels are always visible (no icon-only tabs).
accessibility.reduced_motion: Media query plus a manual toggle (see motion); every animated element has a static counterpart that carries the same information.

weaknesses: The approved character asks for crimson AND semantic red, gold AND semantic amber; the pairs are hue neighbours (rose/coral 1.39:1, gold/amber 1.10:1). The panel separates them by construction, fill and label, which is sound for colour-blind users but means a first-time operator must learn "crimson square = write, coral lamp = failed"; a Settings legend is needed and is not in the size estimate.

Nine reserved hues (acc, read, mut, pub/gold, warn, sent, ok, bad) are more than an operator learns in a session; the labels, glyphs and mode strips carry the meaning, but the colour system is only "obvious" once those are read.

The parchment publish surface is the boldest move: it is the only light surface in a dark UI, which is exactly why it is unmistakable, but on a bright desktop in the light theme it is 1.19:1 against white and depends on its 2px border and crimson offset; the light theme is compliant, not striking.

Without the mockup's illustrations the Command Center is more austere than the approved image; the CSS wash, wordmark and lane glyphs give atmosphere but the director may judge it under-branded and ask for a vector wordmark or a lazily loaded art bundle, both of which are separate decisions with bundle-size consequences (R-06).

Dense, dark, 15px-with-12px-floor layouts get tight at 390px with Android font scaling above 130%; the item track's 26px segments and the three-line rows will wrap earlier than today's two-line rows. Needs a real-device smoke, which planning cannot perform.

Replacing window.confirm (app.mjs:172-175) with a custom sheet is an interaction change, not only a style change: it makes app.confirm asynchronous and touches every call site in screens.mjs; the user must accept that, and it needs its own tests.

CSS transitions on the item track are only meaningful if the run screen stops being rebuilt every 1.5s (app.mjs:268 + dom.mjs:27); that is a rendering-strategy change with its own risk, or the track goes static (which this direction tolerates but which loses one of its few permitted flourishes).

The running sweep is the one continuous animation; if it were ever left running after a pause it would misreport state, so it must be bound to app.state.running and covered by a test, and reduced-motion users get no continuous "alive" cue beyond the RUNNING lamp.
Mixed geometry (three square ink controls inside an otherwise 6-8px rounded system) needs discipline in review: one more square-cornered button anywhere dilutes the rule.
Whether Firefox Android forwards prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme from Samsung system settings is unverified from source; the manual toggles cover it but add two settings.
SVG glyphs drawn in code add JS bytes and an icon map to maintain; Unicode glyphs were rejected because coverage on the Samsung system font could not be proven from the repository.
